headline: The Soccer / Fútbol Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet your team, give times and scores, describe how you feel, say what gear you need, ask simple questions and ask for help, and start Soccer / Fútbol Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Greet teammates and coaches and say basic soccer words with clear Spanish sounds.
lessons.focus: The five pure vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent; greetings at practice

words.note: The written accent puts the stress on the last syllable: ba-LÓN.
ch sounds like English 'church'.
j is a strong, breathy h: hoo-gah-DOR. A woman is la jugadora.
Keep vowels short and pure: eh-KEE-poh.
The accent marks the stress: ÁR-bi-tro.
ll sounds like English y in 'yes': ro-DEE-ya.
In Mexico la barra is the organized group of fans. In South America barra brava means violent hooligans, so use afición for fans in general.
A woman is la entrenadora.
Players in Mexico often call the coach profe.
Informal (tú), between teammates. To an adult you don't know, say ¿Cómo está?

words.en: Nice to meet you, I'm on the team.
How do you say "ball" in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Greet a teammate before practice, say your name, and ask how to say one piece of gear in Spanish.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Say match times, scores, jersey numbers, laps and minutes left in a game or practice.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and soccer quantities: minutes, laps, yards and scores

words.note: Also your jersey number.
US fields and drills are often marked in yards.
Use el for 'on': el domingo = on Sunday.

words.en: The match is at 10 in the morning.
words.es: El partido es a las 10 de la mañana.

words.note: Say it as las seis y media.

words.en: We're going to run 4 laps around the field.
words.es: Vamos a dar 4 vueltas a la cancha.
words.note: Ustedes command, from the coach to the whole team.

lessons.speaking: Tell a teammate what time the match is, what number you wear, and how many minutes are left.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Describe players and the field: who someone is, how you feel and what condition the field is in.
lessons.focus: ser for who or what someone is; estar for how they feel, field conditions and location

words.note: A woman says cansada.
Estar listo = to be ready. A woman says lista.
A woman says lesionada.
On the field, solo means no defender is near you.
A woman is la capitana.
A woman is la portera.
estar: a condition that can change.
A woman says cansada and lista.

words.es: Ella es la capitana del equipo.
words.note: ser: who someone is.
Shout it to get the ball. A woman says ¡Estoy sola!

words.en: The coach is on the bench.
words.es: El entrenador está en la banca.
words.note: estar: location.

lessons.speaking: Tell your coach how you feel today (tired, ready or nervous) and say whether the field is wet.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what gear you have, what you need and want, and what everyone has to bring.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive with soccer gear

words.note: Common word in Mexico and the US; some players say los zapatos de fútbol.
Mexican usage.

words.en: I have my cleats in my backpack.
words.es: Tengo mis tacos en la mochila.

words.en: Is there water on the bench?
words.note: hay = there is / there are, for one or many.

words.en: I need the ball pump, please.
I want to play goalkeeper today.
You have to wear shin guards.
words.note: hay que + infinitive = everyone has to do it.
Informal (tú), between teammates.

lessons.speaking: Tell the coach what gear you have and what you need, and ask a teammate if there is water on the bench.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you are going to do in practice and what you can or can't do.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer, and poder for practice and match plans

words.note: Common in the US and Mexico.
In Mexico camión means bus, not truck.

words.en: I'm going to the stadium by bus.
words.note: a + el = al.

words.en: We're going to do the warm-up.
words.note: ir a + infinitive = a plan.
Informal (tú), between teammates.

words.en: Today we're going to practice shots.
I can't go to practice tomorrow.
words.es: No puedo ir a la práctica mañana.

lessons.speaking: Tell a teammate where you are going after practice and what you are going to do tomorrow, and ask if they can play Saturday.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Talk about what you and your team do every week with regular present-tense verbs.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs for yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos

words.note: A woman is la compañera.
-er verb, yo: corr-o.

words.en: Do you practice with the team on Tuesdays?
words.note: -ar verb, tú: practic-as.

words.en: You coach my son's team, right?
words.es: Usted entrena al equipo de mi hijo, ¿verdad?
words.note: -ar verb, usted: entren-a. Formal, to a coach you don't know well.

words.en: We receive the ball with our chest.
words.es: Recibimos el balón con el pecho.
words.note: -ir verb, nosotros: recib-imos.
-ir verb, ellos: viv-en.

lessons.speaking: Tell a new teammate what days you practice, how often you run, and which foot you pass with.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask teammates, coaches and fans simple questions about who, where, when and how much.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué and cuál at the field

words.note: ¿cuántos? for how many: ¿Cuántos jugadores hay?
Two words in a question; porque (one word) means because.
Use cuál before es for 'what is': ¿Cuál es tu número?

words.en: How much is the team jersey?

lessons.speaking: Ask a teammate who the referee is, where the locker room is, and when the next match starts.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody and not yet on the field, and ask for more, less or another.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro in practice and match talk

words.note: Never use un before otro: otro balón, not un otro balón.
A woman is la suplente.

words.en: I never play without shin guards.
Today we talk less and run more.
words.es: Hoy hablamos menos y corremos más.
words.note: Ustedes commands, from the coach to the team.
Common way to say no problem or don't worry.

lessons.speaking: Tell your coach you are not ready yet, say that nobody is in the goal, and ask if there is another ball.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Politely ask a coach, trainer or fan for help and give simple usted commands.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands for everyday verbs at the field and stadium

words.note: Feminine even though it ends in -o: la foto.

words.en: Can you pass me the towel, please?
words.note: ¿Puede + infinitive? is a polite usted request.
Usted command: traer becomes traiga.

words.es: Espere en la banca, por favor.

words.en: Can you take a photo of us?
Excuse me, can you tell me where my seat is?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿puede decirme dónde está mi asiento?

lessons.speaking: Politely ask the team trainer for the towel and ice, and ask a fan at the stadium to take a photo of you.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Use Spanish words you already know and ask for help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, and survival phrases for the field

words.note: -ción often matches English -tion.
Means excitement or emotion, a common word for big match moments.
-dad often matches English -ty, but not always.
-ente often matches English -ent.

words.en: I don't understand, can you repeat?

words.note: Ustedes command, to everyone nearby in an emergency.

words.en: It's a great opportunity for the team.
words.es: Es una gran oportunidad para el equipo.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coach you speak a little Spanish, ask them to repeat more slowly, and say what is important in your position.
